title: Gambas al Ajillo
subtitle: Spanish garlic prawns sizzling in olive oil and chilli
excerpt: Gambas al ajillo is one of the most famous Spanish tapas: raw prawns cooked at the table in a glazed terracotta dish of olive oil, sliced garlic, dried chilli, and sherry. The prawns take 3 minutes to cook. The sizzling oil is mopped up with crusty bread.
sourceNotes: Gambas al ajillo (garlic prawns) is a classic of Spanish tapa culture, found throughout the country but particularly associated with Madrid and the coastal regions. The word 'gambas' refers to large prawns; smaller shrimp are not used. The dish is traditionally cooked and served in a small terracotta or cast-iron dish.

content.text: Use large raw prawns with their shells on if possible. The shells protect the meat from overcooking and add flavour to the oil. The dish is cooked very fast over very high heat. If using sherry, add it after the prawns are in and step back from the pan: it will spit.

items.prepNote: thinly sliced, or 1 dried chilli crumbled

content.text: Heat the olive oil in a heavy frying pan or small cast-iron dish over high heat until it shimmers. Add the garlic slices and chilli. Cook for 30 seconds until the garlic begins to turn golden at the edges. Do not let it brown fully or it will be bitter.

Add the prawns in a single layer. Season with salt. Cook for 1 minute without moving. Flip. Cook for 1 more minute until the prawns are pink and just curled. Do not overcook. They continue cooking in the residual hot oil.
Scatter with parsley. Add a squeeze of lemon if you like. Serve immediately in the pan with crusty bread.

items.fix: Prawns cook in 2 minutes maximum at high heat. They are done when pink and curled. Pull them the moment they lose their raw grey colour.
